function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

message.content: Below is a **step‑by‑step playbook** you can follow to build a modern, production‑ready frontend for an e‑commerce site. I’ll cover the whole stack (design → code → deployment) and give you concrete examples, best‑practice tips, and links to the most popular tools. --- ## 1. Define the Scope & Gather Requirements | Item | Why it matters | How to capture it | |------|----------------|-------------------| | **Core features** | Product catalog, search, filters, cart, checkout, user accounts, reviews, admin panel | User stories, MoSCoW prioritisation | | **Target devices** | Desktop, tablet, mobile, PWA | Responsive design, mobile‑first approach | | **Performance goals** | First paint < 1 s, interactive < 2 s | Lighthouse audit, Web Vitals | | **SEO & Accessibility** | Google ranking, WCAG 2.1 AA | Meta tags, semantic HTML, ARIA | | **Analytics & Tracking** | Conversion funnels, heatmaps | GA4, Hotjar, Mixpanel | | **Compliance** | GDPR, PCI‑DSS | Consent banner, secure payment flow | > **Tip:** Create a *feature matrix* (feature × device) to visualise coverage early. --- ## 2. Choose the Tech Stack | Layer | Options | Recommendation | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Framework** | React, Vue, Angular, Svelte | **React + Next.js** (SSR + SSG + API routes) | | **Styling** | CSS Modules, Tailwind CSS, Styled‑Components | **Tailwind CSS** (utility‑first, fast prototyping) | | **State** | Redux Toolkit, Zustand, React Query | **React Query** for server state + **Zustand** for UI state | | **Component Library** | Material‑UI, Ant Design, Chakra UI | **Chakra UI** (accessibility out‑of‑the‑box) | | **Testing** | Jest, React Testing Library, Cypress | Unit + E2E: Jest + Cypress | | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Vercel | **GitHub Actions** + **Vercel** (auto‑deploy preview) | | **Hosting** | Vercel, Netlify, AWS Amplify | **Vercel** (Next.js first‑class support) | | **Analytics** | GA4, Plausible, Segment | **GA4** + **Plausible** (privacy‑friendly) | | **Payment** | Stripe, PayPal, Braintree | **Stripe** (modern API, strong docs) | > **Why Next.js?** > • Built‑in SSR/SSG → instant page loads & SEO. > • API routes → you can keep the same repo for both frontend & backend logic. > • Image optimisation, routing, environment variables baked in. --- ## 3. Design & Prototyping 1. **Wireframes** – Sketch low‑fidelity screens for each page (Home, Category, Product, Cart, Checkout, Account). 2. **High‑fidelity mockups** – Use Figma or Adobe XD. 3. **Design System** – Define colors, typography, spacing, component patterns. 4. **Accessibility audit** – Check contrast, keyboard navigation, screen‑reader labels. > **Tool:** Figma + FigJam for collaborative design; export assets as SVG/PNG. --- ## 4. Project Skeleton (Next.js + Tailwind + Chakra) ```bash npx create-next-app@latest ecommerce-frontend cd ecommerce-frontend npm install tailwindcss@latest postcss@latest autoprefixer@latest npx tailwindcss init -p npm install @chakra-ui/react @emotion/react @emotion/styled framer-motion npm install react-query zustand ``` **`tailwind.config.js`** ```js module.exports = { content: [ "./pages/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}", "./components/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}", ], theme: { extend: {}, }, plugins: [], } ``` **`pages/_app.tsx`** ```tsx import { ChakraProvider } from "@chakra-ui/react"; import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "react-query"; import { Provider as StoreProvider } from "zustand"; import store from "../store"; const queryClient = new QueryClient(); export default function App({ Component, pageProps }) { return ( ); } ``` --- ## 5. Core Components (Illustrative) ### 5.1 Product Card ```tsx // components/ProductCard.tsx import { Box, Image, Text, Button } from "@chakra-ui/react"; import Link from "next/link"; export default function ProductCard({ product }) { return ( {product.title} ${product.price} ); } ``` ### 5.2 Cart Context (Zustand) ```ts // store/cart.ts import create from "zustand"; export const useCartStore = create((set) => ({ items: [], addItem: (item) => set((state) => ({ items: [...state.items, item] })), removeItem: (id) => set((state) => ({ items: state.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) })), clear: () => set({ items: [] }), })); ``` ### 5.3 Data Fetching (React Query) ```tsx // hooks/useProducts.ts import { useQuery } from "react-query"; import axios from "axios"; export const fetchProducts = async () => { const { data } = await axios.get("/api/products"); return data; }; export const useProducts = () => useQuery("products", fetchProducts); ``` --- ## 6. Routing & Pages | Page | Path | Notes | |------|------|-------| | Home | `/` | Show featured products, hero banner | | Category | `/category/[slug]` | Dynamic route, filter by category | | Product | `/product/[slug]` | SSR for SEO, fetch product details | | Cart | `/cart` | Client‑side only, uses Zustand | | Checkout | `/checkout` | Protected route, Stripe integration | | Account | `/account` | Auth‑protected, profile & order history | | Admin | `/admin/*` | Separate layout, role‑based access | > **Tip:** Use `getStaticProps` + `getStaticPaths` for product pages to pre‑render them at build time. --- ## 7. API Integration ### 7.1 Backend API (Next.js API Routes) ```ts // pages/api/products.ts import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from "next"; import { getAllProducts } from "../../lib/db"; export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) { const products = await getAllProducts(); res.status(200).json(products); } ``` > **Alternative:** If you already have a separate backend (Node, Django, etc.), consume it via REST or GraphQL. ### 7.2 Payment Flow (Stripe) ```tsx // pages/checkout.tsx import { loadStripe } from "@stripe/stripe-js"; import { Elements } from "@stripe/react-stripe-js"; import CheckoutForm from "../components/CheckoutForm"; const stripePromise = loadStripe(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!); export default function Checkout() { return ( ); } ``` --- ## 8. Performance Optimisation | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | **Image optimisation** | Next.js `` component, `next/image` | | **Code splitting** | Automatic with Next.js | | **Lazy loading** | `loading="lazy"` on images, dynamic imports | | **Prefetching** | `next/link` prefetch | | **Caching** | CDN (Vercel), HTTP cache headers | | **Critical CSS** | Tailwind purge, `next/font` for fonts | | **Bundle size** | `next-bundle-analyzer` plugin | Run `npm run lint` and `npm run build && npm run start` to check bundle size and Lighthouse scores. --- ## 9. Testing Strategy | Layer | Tool | Focus | |-------|------|-------| | Unit | Jest + React Testing Library | Component logic, hooks | | Integration | Cypress | End‑to‑end flows (login, add to cart, checkout) | | Visual | Percy | UI regression | | Accessibility | axe-core | WCAG compliance | > **Example test** – `components/__tests__/ProductCard.test.tsx` ```tsx import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react"; import ProductCard from "../ProductCard"; test("renders product title and price", () => { const product = { title: "Test Shirt", price: 29.99, image: "/shirt.png", slug: "test-shirt" }; render(); expect(screen.getByText("Test Shirt")).toBeInTheDocument(); expect(screen.getByText("$29.99")).toBeInTheDocument(); }); ``` --- ## 10. Deployment & CI/CD 1. **Push to GitHub** – Branch `main` triggers deployment. 2. **GitHub Actions** – Example workflow: ```yaml name: CI/CD on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: branches: [main] jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: 20 - run: npm ci - run: npm run build - uses: vercel/action@v1 with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} ``` 3. **Environment Variables** – Store secrets in Vercel dashboard (`NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, etc.). --- ## 11. Post‑Launch Checklist | Item | Action | |------|--------| | **Analytics** | Verify GA4 events, set up conversion goals | | **SEO** | Submit sitemap, check robots.txt | | **Accessibility** | Run axe audit, fix issues | | **Performance** | Monitor Lighthouse, set up Sentry for errors | | **Security** | Enable CSP, HTTPS, HSTS | | **Backup** | Regular database snapshots | | **Monitoring** | UptimeRobot, New Relic | --- ## 12. Resources & Further Reading | Topic | Link | |-------|------| | Next.js Docs | https://nextjs.org/docs | | Tailwind CSS Docs | https://tailwindcss.com/docs | | Chakra UI Docs | https://chakra-ui.com/docs | | React Query Docs | https://react-query.tanstack.com/ | | Stripe Checkout | https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout | | Lighthouse Audits | https://developers.google.com/web/tools/lighthouse | | Accessibility Checklist | https://deque.com/blog/10-ways-to-improve-web-accessibility | --- ### Quick Recap 1. **Plan** → define features, target devices, performance goals. 2. **Design** → wireframes → high‑fidelity mockups → design system. 3. **Build** → Next.js + Tailwind + Chakra + React Query + Zustand. 4. **Integrate** → API routes or external backend, Stripe. 5. **Test** → Jest + Cypress. 6. **Deploy** → Vercel + GitHub Actions. 7. **Monitor** → Analytics, performance, security. Follow this roadmap, tweak the stack to fit your team’s expertise, and you’ll have a scalable, maintainable e‑commerce frontend in a few weeks. Happy coding!
